description: Potential data race: shared mutable state across threads
rationale: Undefined behavior in Rust/MAGE
fix_template: Wrap in Mutex, RwLock, or use Atomic types

description: Potential deadlock: lock ordering violation
rationale: Two locks acquired in different orders across threads

description: Type not Send — cannot be transferred between threads
rationale: Type contains non-thread-safe internals (Rc, raw pointers)
fix_template: Use Arc instead of Rc; ensure all fields are Send

description: Type not Sync — cannot be shared between threads via &
rationale: Type allows mutation through shared reference without synchronization
fix_template: Wrap in Mutex for synchronized access

description: Mutex may be poisoned after panic in another thread
rationale: lock() returns Err if holder panicked

description: RwLock may cause writer starvation under heavy read load
rationale: Many readers can block writers indefinitely

description: Channel recv() may fail if all senders dropped
rationale: Disconnected channel returns RecvError

description: Arc<Mutex<T>> is the standard shared mutable state pattern
rationale: Arc for shared ownership, Mutex for interior mutability

description: Incorrect atomic memory ordering may cause subtle bugs
rationale: Use SeqCst when unsure; Relaxed only for counters

description: Spawned thread requires 'static or scoped thread
rationale: std::thread::spawn requires 'static closure

description: Blocking in async runtime blocks the executor thread
rationale: Use spawn_blocking() for blocking operations

description: Using std::sync::Mutex in async; prefer tokio::sync::Mutex
rationale: std Mutex blocks the thread; tokio Mutex yields

description: tokio::select! is not fair — first ready branch wins
rationale: Under contention, some branches may starve

description: Async operation not cancellation-safe in select!
rationale: Partial progress lost when branch is cancelled

description: Rayon parallel iterators require Send + Sync bounds
rationale: Data must be safely shareable for parallelism

description: Global mutable state requires synchronization
rationale: static mut is unsafe; use Mutex<T> or atomics
fix_template: Use std::sync::OnceLock or Lazy for initialization

description: crossbeam::scope allows non-'static references in threads
rationale: Scoped threads join before scope ends, ensuring lifetimes

description: Use OnceLock/LazyLock for thread-safe lazy initialization
rationale: Initialized at most once; safe to share across threads

description: Barrier synchronizes N threads at a rendezvous point
rationale: All threads wait until the last one arrives

description: Condvar allows waiting for a condition with a Mutex
rationale: Use with Mutex for efficient event waiting

description: Consider parking_lot::Mutex for better performance
rationale: Faster than std Mutex in many workloads

description: Work-stealing scheduler distributes tasks across threads
rationale: Rayon and Tokio use work-stealing for load balancing

description: Futures must be Pinned before polling
rationale: Async state machines contain self-references

description: Future not Send — cannot be spawned on multi-threaded runtime
rationale: Future holds non-Send types across await
fix_template: Clone data before await or use single-threaded runtime

description: Unbounded channel can grow without limit
rationale: Memory usage grows if consumer is slower than producer

description: Actor model: each actor has private state, communicates via messages
rationale: Avoids shared state; good for concurrency

description: Semaphore limits concurrent access to a resource
rationale: Allows N concurrent holders

description: Lock-free data structures use atomics instead of locks
rationale: Avoids blocking but complex to implement correctly

description: RwLock read lock inside write lock causes deadlock on some platforms
rationale: Re-entrant read inside write blocks forever
fix_template: Avoid acquiring read lock while holding write lock

description: thread_local! provides per-thread storage without synchronization
rationale: Each thread has its own copy

description: Volatile access for memory-mapped I/O: std::ptr::read_volatile
rationale: Prevents compiler from optimizing away reads/writes

description: Spinlock wastes CPU cycles; prefer Mutex for general use
rationale: Spinning is only appropriate for very short critical sections

description: Async task spawn is cheaper than OS thread spawn
rationale: Use tasks for fine-grained concurrency

description: Prefer structured concurrency: spawn tasks in a scope
rationale: JoinSet/TaskGroup ensure all tasks complete before proceeding
fix_template: Use JoinSet to manage spawned tasks

description: Priority inversion: high-priority thread waits on low-priority holding lock
rationale: OS scheduling anomaly with locks
